newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia says economic ties unaffected by row.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says economic ties unaffected by row.

text.p: Malaysia on Thursday said that tourism, cultural and sporting links with Singapore have been suspended, but commercial ties between two closely linked economies would not be affected.

Malaysia's cabinet decided at a meeting on Wednesday to suspend cultural, tourism and sporting contacts with Singapore for the time being, the national news agency Bernama quoted Culture, Arts and Tourism Minister Sabbaruddin Chik as saying.
"From our discussions (in the cabinet), the question of trade did not arise. There's no ban, there are no restrictions," Sabbaruddin told Bernama.
But he said culture, tourism and sporting contacts would be affected. "If we have any sporting activities with them, then it will be suspended," Sabbarruddin was quoted as saying.
"In this regard, the Singapore-Malaysia joint committee on tourism, which meets occasionally depending on the need, will be suspended until there is a decision otherwise," he said.

He was clarifying Malaysian media reports on Thursday that quoted him and several other unidentified ministers as saying the government had decided to freeze all new bilateral dealings with Singapore to protest derogatory comments about a southern Malaysian state by Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew.
Mahathir told a news conference in Tokyo the issue was not a major problem and would be overcome with time.
Gingerly stepping around the cabinet decision, Mahathir made clear, however, that Lee's remarks still rankled Malaysians.
"I would like to know more about this before I explain the reason why. They (cabinet ministers) must have had some reason for making this decision," he said.
"But I don't think this is a major problem," Mahathir said on the second day of a four-day visit to Japan.
Media reports said Malaysia was freezing ties with Singapore, including the awarding of new contracts to Singapore firms.
But in Kuala Lumpur on Thursday, Malaysian Minister of Works S. Samy Vellu said only a culture and sports agreement was suspended.
Acting foreign minister Abang Abu Bakar Abang Mustapha said "no decision has been made to freeze ties with Singapore as reported by the local newspapers."
The row began after Lee, in a court affidavit leaked to the Malaysian press, described the southern Malaysian state of Johor as "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings".

Lee apologised and instructed his lawyer to ask the court to delete the remarks from a deposition in a libel suit against a Singaporean opposition politician who fled to Johor after saying he had received death threats in Singapore.
Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong held his opinion on the matter.
"I think I want to take some time to understand Malaysia's reaction before I comment," he told reporters on Thursday after talks with visiting Australian Prime Minister John Howard.
"I want to absorb the implications of all this before I give my comments," Goh said.
During a visit to Laos earlier this week, Goh had said it was time for Singapore and Malaysia "to move on" after Malaysia accepted Lee's "unreserved apology".
"There is a Malay saying that water cannot be separated, even with a knife. This is the nature of our relations with Malaysia," he was quoted as saying in Laos by Singapore media.
